story_type: three single-engine air tankers make back to back water drops on a grass wildfire
hook: Three air tankers, one after another, into the smoke.
narration: Three air tankers dove into the smoke, one after another.
The Sutherland Canyon Fire had burned thirty-seven thousand acres in central Washington.
Lightning started it in the grass near the Columbia River.
These are single-engine air tankers. They carry water or retardant, and today it was water.
The next one came in right behind it.
Then another, low through the smoke.
outcome: All three tankers made their water drops on the Sutherland Canyon Fire.
title: Three air tankers dive into a wildfire
description:
On June 28, 2017, three single-engine air tankers made consecutive water drops on the 37,000-acre Sutherland Canyon Fire in central Washington, a lightning-started grass fire near the Columbia River.
